subject: Capacity runway checklist + fallback options for AuroraCode (late-stage)
body:
From: Stephen Cole <stephen@auroracode.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Torres <lina@auroracode.com>, procurement@auroracode.com
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 14:03:00 -0000
Subject: Request: provisional capacity runway for AuroraCode deal

Hannah / Logan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward an internal procurement vote next Wednesday, Procurement has asked us to document an internal capacity plan and request a short provisional hold so we can align SLA language with expected capacity.

Key asks:
- Can Redwood provision a provisional runway of 12 x A100 80GB equivalents (or H100 equiv) for an initial production deployment window (estimated go-live: 2028-11-01)?
- We expect a peak of ~250 qps at 512 tokens with typical burst patterns (see attached traffic_profile_q3.csv).
- We will sign a 12-month Dedicated contract if the procurement committee has reasonable assurance (written) about capacity and fallback options.

Attached: Aurora_PO_estimate.pdf (draft), traffic_profile_q3.csv

Quick note: Procurement wants a named contact in Capacity Ops and any constraints on burst/standby pools. Can you confirm next steps and timeline for a provisional hold?

—Stephen
Stephen Cole
Head of AI Platforms, AuroraCode

---

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Stephen Cole <stephen@auroracode.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 17:08:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: provisional capacity runway for AuroraCode deal

Hi Stephen —

Thanks for the clear ask and the traffic profile. We can support this; want to map expectations so we give Procurement what they need. Short answers up front:
- We can propose a provisional runway for 12 x A100-80GB equivalent nodes, subject to fleet availability at time of commitment.
- We can also document fallback options (quantized LLM variant + autoscale to burst pool) to reduce the hard node requirement in case of supply constraints.

Logan / Priyom / Grace — can Capacity / Fleet confirm current availability across our US regions and whether we can place a soft hold (30 days, non-binding) on 12 A100-eq nodes for AuroraCode with a target go-live date of 2028-11-01? Please include expected procurement timelines for buying down to H100s or L40E fallbacks.

I’ll prepare a short one-page runway checklist for Procurement once we have fleet confirmation.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

---

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephen Cole <stephen@auroracode.com>, Lina Torres <lina@auroracode.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: provisional capacity runway for AuroraCode deal

Hannah / team —

Quick inventory check against current US fleet (summary):
- Available cold stock: 40 x A100-80GB equiv (usable across clusters, 2-day provisioning lead for dedicated carve-outs).
- Available warm nodes (already in reserved pools): 18 x A100-eq (need migration to Dedicated, estimated 7–10 day lead).
- H100 equivalents: limited (8 nodes in us-west), can convert some A100 capacity but will require image/kernel adjustments (3–5 day effort).
- Burst pool (multi-tenant hosted): effectively unlimited for small spikes but not SLA-backed; acceptable as an operational fallback.

Risk notes:
- Commitment by AuroraCode for 12 nodes is fine today if they accept a 30-day soft hold (non-binding). If they want a hard reserve tied to contract signature we need a 4–6 week lead to re-image and reserve capacity.
- If we need to guarantee <50ms p50 latency at 512 tokens, we should target H100-class nodes or additional headroom (14–16 nodes).

Actionable ask: Priyom — please raise a soft-hold ticket and mark nodes for AuroraCode (12 A100-eq). Include fallback policy: 1) quantized 4-bit model variant on 12 L40-series nodes (if A100/H100 unavailable), 2) auto-fallback to burst pool for <10% of traffic. Also include expected cost deltas.

Logan
Logan Wright
Capacity Ops — Redwood Inference

---

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephen Cole <stephen@auroracode.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Sep 2028 11:33:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: provisional capacity runway for AuroraCode deal

Folks —

Soft-hold ticket raised: RHW-75412 (internal). Summary of steps taken and current status:
- 12 x A100-80GB-equivalent nodes tentatively reserved in us-east with a soft hold window: 2028-09-15 -> 2028-10-15.
- Hold is non-binding — we will release automatically on 2028-10-15 unless a formal capacity reservation request is received.
- Cost delta note: moving to a hard Dedicated reservation increases monthly cost by ~18% over provisional pricing (this is included in the attached estimate).

Fallback options documented in the ticket:
- Quantized model variant (4-bit) on 12 x L40E nodes — expected ~1.7x inference latency vs A100 but 0.45x cost.
- Hybrid approach: 8 Dedicated A100-eq + 4 burst-enabled nodes to reduce the hard-node ask and maintain SLA via overprovisioning during peak.

Requested items from AuroraCode for the invoice and procurement packet:
1) Signed PO or a scanned letter of intent (LOI) by 2028-09-30 to extend the soft hold beyond 10/15.
2) Confirmation of desired SLA (p50/p95 latencies) and whether a failure-tolerant fallback (burst pool) is acceptable.

Ticket link (internal): https://internal.redwood.com/rhw/tickets/RHW-75412

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Capacity Planning — Redwood Inference

Attachment stub: [Attachment: RHW-75412-hold-summary.txt]

---

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Stephen Cole <stephen@auroracode.com>, Lina Torres <lina@auroracode.com>, procurement@auroracode.com
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Sep 2028 16:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Capacity runway checklist + fallback options for AuroraCode (late-stage)

Stephen / Lina / Procurement team —

Following up with the runway checklist and clear next steps so Procurement can close the packet:

1) Current status (short): 12 x A100-80GB-eq soft hold placed in us-east via ticket RHW-75412. Soft hold window: 2028-09-15 -> 2028-10-15.
2) Required by Procurement to extend hold: signed PO or LOI by 2028-09-30.
3) Fallback options we recommend (documented in the ticket):
   - Primary: Dedicated reservation of 12 A100-eq nodes (4–6 week lead for hard reserve).
   - Fallback A: Quantized model on 12 x L40E nodes (cost savings but higher tail latency).
   - Fallback B: Hybrid 8 Dedicated A100-eq + 4 burst pool nodes (keeps costs and latency balanced).
4) SLA guidance: If AuroraCode requires p50 < 50ms at 512 tokens we recommend H100-class or additional headroom. Please indicate target latencies in the PO.
5) Contacts: Logan Wright (Capacity Ops) — logan.wright@redwood.com; Priyom Das (Capacity Planning) — priyom.das@redwood.com.

Stephen — once you confirm which fallback you accept (A/B/none) and either upload a signed LOI or PO to the DocuSign link we shared, we will extend the hold window and begin hard-reserve planning if needed.

Thanks — appreciate the partnership here.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | https://www.redwood.com
